deals.travelWindow: Oct 3 – Dec 6, cheapest early October and December
deals.whyRanked: Allegiant's fare calendar still shows sub-$70 one-ways (Oct 3, Nov 14, Dec 6) for a $124-136 round trip — a modest bump from last week's $118, but still a near-tie for cheapest and the closest national park of the five keeps it on top.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's compact grid is easy to explore alone on foot, and the Cosby and Greenbrier entrances to the Smokies are a short solo drive with none of the Cades Cove crowds.

highlights: Market Square street music and farmers' stalls
Ijams Nature Center quarry swimming hole
Great Smoky Mountains NP's Cosby entrance
itinerary: Day 1 — Arrive, Sunsphere deck at golden hour, dinner and live music on Market Square.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Cosby: Hen Wallow Falls trail, then loop the Foothills Parkway for sunset views.
Day 3 — Ijams Nature Center swim and trails in the morning, Knoxville Museum of Art before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown and Ijams are walkable or a short rideshare apart; a rental car is required to reach the national park.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near Market Square or Gay Street — walkable to restaurants and the Tennessee Theatre.

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's own fare calendar keeps showing $59 one-ways scattered across Oct, Nov, and Dec — the cheapest confirmed floor of the week, and DC still carries the strongest solo score of the five.
deals.soloWhy: The Metro reaches nearly every monument and museum, the Mall is safe to walk solo well into the evening, and the Smithsonians are free.

highlights: National Mall monuments lit up after dark
Great Falls Park overlook on the Potomac
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, drop bags, U.S. Botanic Garden before close, then the Mall monuments once they're lit and quiet.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Shenandoah: Skyline Drive to Hawksbill summit, back for an H Street dinner.
Day 3 — Great Falls Park towpath walk in the morning, Eastern Market for lunch before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Metro covers the Mall, museums, and most neighborhoods; a rental car is only needed for Shenandoah or Great Falls.
guide.stayArea: Near a Metro stop on the Orange/Blue/Silver line (Capitol Hill or Foggy Bottom) for the fastest reach to the Mall.

deals.whyRanked: Southwest's fare calendar still confirms $59 one-way basic fares each direction (Oct 20-22) — unchanged for three weeks running, and Southwest's free 2-bag allowance keeps stretching the basic fare further.
deals.soloWhy: The Inner Harbor and Fells Point are flat, walkable, and full of counter-seating spots that make solo dining easy, with a water taxi linking the neighborhoods.

itinerary: Day 1 — Inner Harbor on arrival, National Aquarium, water taxi to Fells Point for oysters at a counter stool.
Day 2 — Fort McHenry in the morning, then a Station North mural walk before dinner in Fells Point.
Day 3 — Baltimore Museum of Art, Lexington Market crab cakes before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Inner Harbor, Fells Point, and Fort McHenry are covered by the water taxi and a short walk or rideshare; no rental car needed unless heading to Assateague.
guide.stayArea: Fells Point or the Inner Harbor — walkable, close to the water taxi and restaurants.

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's fall flash sale still shows one-ways from $99 (Nov 3-4) and $119 (Oct 21) — pricier than the FL/TX picks, but Rocky Mountain National Park's 90-minute drive and a perfect solo score push Denver back into the top 5.
deals.soloWhy: A dense downtown hostel and brewery scene, easy A Line rail from the airport, and trailheads that are simple to reach solo without a group make Denver one of the easiest cities to travel alone.

highlights: RiNo Art District murals and breweries
Larimer Square and Union Station's Great Hall
Rocky Mountain National Park's Bear Lake corridor
itinerary: Day 1 — A Line train into Union Station, wander Larimer Square, RiNo brewery crawl at dusk.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Rocky Mountain NP: Bear Lake Road to Dream Lake or Emerald Lake, drive back for a Highlands dinner.
Day 3 — Denver Art Museum in the morning, Red Rocks at sunset before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The A Line train connects the airport straight to Union Station, and RTD light rail covers downtown and the Highlands; a rental car is only needed for Rocky Mountain NP or Red Rocks.
guide.stayArea: LoDo (Lower Downtown) near Union Station — walkable to Larimer Square, the train, and RiNo.

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's calendar still shows $80 one-ways (Oct 24, Nov 14/17/18) and $120 in December — cheaper than Denver on paper, but a shorter solo-nature draw and a smaller park boost keep it at fifth.
deals.soloWhy: The beachfront promenade and Las Olas strip stay lively and well-lit into the evening, and the free Sun Trolley makes getting around solo simple without a car.

itinerary: Day 1 — Check in near the beach, promenade walk at sunset, dinner and people-watching on Las Olas.
Day 2 — Drive to Shark Valley: rent a bike for the flat 15-mile Everglades loop, alligators basking along the canal.
Day 3 — Bonnet House gardens and Riverwalk in the morning before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free Sun Trolley covers downtown, Las Olas, and the beach; a rental car is worth it only for the Everglades day trip.
guide.stayArea: The beachfront or Las Olas — both walkable to restaurants, the promenade, and water taxi stops.
